proposals.correctedText: Research in ISSCR category 2 requires review and approval through a specialised scientific and ethics review process.
proposals.rationale: The consent-scope requirement was not located in the inspected sections and is not carried by the categories.

proposals.correctedText: Classify research activities by the level of oversight they require, following ISSCR categories 1A to 3B.
proposals.rationale: It classifies research activities by required oversight, not materials, data and dual-use risk as four separate axes. The page states a broader taxonomy than the source operates.

proposals.correctedText: Work under an appropriate oversight mechanism with a defined endpoint.
proposals.rationale: Retention, sharing and disposal were not located in the inspected sections.

proposals.correctedText: Responsible biocomputing governance begins before acquisitio [Stated as this page's own working formulation; no inspected source establishes it.]
proposals.rationale: ISSCR sets oversight expectations for stem cell research. It does not state a biocomputing governance lifecycle running from acquisition through communication, and the page presents that lifecycle as established practice. The framing may be reasonable; it is not what this source says.

proposals.correctedText: An empirical claim predicts observable differences under spe [Stated as this page's own working formulation; no inspected source establishes it.]
proposals.rationale: A definition of what an empirical claim is. PRISMA defines reporting items, not epistemology, and no inspected source states this definition.

proposals.correctedText: When reporting a systematic review, PRISMA 2020 requires results and limitations to be reported under its Results and Discussion items.
proposals.rationale: It governs the reporting of systematic reviews, not the reporting of a primary study. The page prescribes study practice generally.

proposals.correctedText: Separate exploratory from confirmatory hypotheses. [This page states this as its own working practice. The source cited for it is a reporting standard that states it must not be used to guide research conduct.]
proposals.rationale: PRISMA 2020 states that it is not intended to guide systematic review conduct. The page cites it behind guidance about how to conduct a study. The source explicitly forbids the use being made of it.

proposals.correctedText: Use appropriate controls and blinded assessment where possib [This page states this as its own working practice. The source cited for it is a reporting standard that states it must not be used to guide research conduct.]
proposals.rationale: Study-conduct guidance behind a reporting standard that states it should not be used to assess the conduct or methodological quality of reviews. Same mismatch as the preceding assertion.

decisionNote: Every decision is recorded as needs-more-evidence. An automated internal reading is not a completed editorial review, and recording it as one would manufacture the approval the canary requires.

previewCanary.reason: Only 0 proposals carry a completed approval. A smaller cohort was not constructed, as instructed, so no Preview canary is prepared.

productionReachability.note: Each proposal was tested against assertMayReachProduction with an authenticated release authority. All were refused, because no decision is approved. Authority alone is not sufficient.

boundary: Proposals only. The active revision of every page is unchanged and every proposal carries active:false with appliesToRelease:null.
